name: Operation of a fibre-pigtailed, bias-tuned quantum-dot micropillar single-photon source in a compact 2.4 K two-stage G-M cryocooler
plain_name: Run a plug-and-play fibre-connected quantum-dot light source inside a compact 2.4 K cooler
description: Margaria et al. (C2N/Quandela) attach a single-mode fibre directly to a deterministic QD micropillar whose p-i-n junction is bias-tuned through electrical contact ridges, then operate it in a rack-mounted compact two-stage Gifford-McMahon cryocooler at 2.4 K for ten-hour stability runs (fibre brightness 20.8%, indistinguishability 97.5%).
keywords: Run a plug-and-play fibre-connected quantum-dot light source inside a compact 2.4 K cooler

sources.citation: Efficient fibre-pigtailed source of indistinguishable single photons (Margaria et al., Nature Communications 16:7553, 2025)

reported_equipment: Single Quantum superconducting nanowires single-photon detectors

requirements.rationale: The pigtailed source was operated at the cryocooler base temperature of 2.4 K (the 5 K free-space setup gave lower indistinguishability).
The QD charge state and emission wavelength are set by a bias voltage through electrical contacts on the chip.
Optional: the deployable source runs in a closed-cycle G-M cryocooler without liquid cryogens.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
